purpose: Define how candidate mechanisms are intended to be used in the research architecture without ranking performance or authorizing promotion.

roles.description: Directly generates a fixed cross-sectional or directional trading hypothesis and therefore requires its own complete coverage, PIT, performance and robustness evidence.
roles.use_rule: Keep treatment and control explicit; no composition until the candidate has its own valid evidence chain.

roles.description: Sparse, timestamp-sensitive public-information events intended to explain or exploit short-horizon information arrival rather than act as an always-on selector.
roles.use_rule: Freeze event definitions and public-availability clocks first; event density/coverage failures are hard stops.

roles.description: Low-frequency institutional and fundamental state variables whose natural holding horizon is slower than daily signal turnover.
roles.use_rule: Treat 13F and N-PORT as distinct information clocks; no pooling of their observations without an explicit join contract.

roles.description: Slow market-wide or cross-asset states that can condition exposure, abstention, or capital allocation without being mistaken for stock-selection alpha.
roles.use_rule: First establish source/PIT feasibility independently; only later test a predeclared overlay/allocator contract.

roles.description: Deterministic downstream combination of already-frozen and independently evidenced components.
roles.use_rule: Never use composition to rescue weak components; component validity comes first.

operating_policy.principle: Prefer a small number of independently validated orthogonal mechanisms over a large stack of correlated hypotheses.
